questions.question_text: In the fraction 3/4, what does the number 4 (the denominator) represent?
options: A) The total number of equal parts the whole is divided into
B) The number of parts selected or shaded
C) The total number of wholes being compared
D) The number 4 has no specific meaning
accepted_answers: The total number of equal parts the whole is divided into
questions.verified_explanation: The denominator indicates the total number of equal-sized parts into which the whole unit is divided.
questions.learning_objective: Identify the denominator as the total number of equal parts dividing the whole.

questions.question_text: A pizza is cut into 3 slices of different sizes. Can one slice be called 1/3 of the pizza?
options: A) Yes, because there are 3 slices in total
B) No, because the slices must be equal in size to be unit fractions
C) Yes, if the pizza is round
D) It depends on whether the pizza has toppings
accepted_answers: No, because the slices must be equal in size to be unit fractions
questions.verified_explanation: Fractions require that the parts dividing the whole be identical in size (fair shares).
questions.learning_objective: Understand that parts of the whole must be equal in size.

options: D) Cannot be determined without a calculator
questions.verified_explanation: Dividing the same whole into 3 equal parts produces larger individual parts than dividing into 5 equal parts. Therefore, 2 thirds (2/3) is greater than 2 fifths (2/5). Alternatively, 2/3 = 10/15 and 2/5 = 6/15, and 10/15 > 6/15.

options: D) 3/8 is larger because 3 is a prime number
questions.verified_explanation: When denominators are identical, the parts are the same size (eighths). Having 5 parts is greater than having 3 parts, so 5/8 > 3/8.
Multiplying both numerator and denominator of 1/2 by 2 yields (1*2)/(2*2) = 2/4. Both represent half of the whole.

questions.question_text: If you add 2 to both the numerator and denominator of 1/3, you get 3/5. Is 3/5 equivalent to 1/3?
options: A) Yes, because you added the same number to top and bottom
B) No, adding the same number changes the value; only multiplying or dividing by the same factor preserves equivalence
C) Yes, both are less than 1
D) Only if the denominator is odd
accepted_answers: No, adding the same number changes the value
questions.verified_explanation: Adding a number to numerator and denominator changes the proportional relationship. 1/3 is approximately 0.333, while 3/5 is 0.6. Equivalence requires multiplication or division by a common non-zero factor.
questions.learning_objective: Recognize invalid additive transformations in fractions.

questions.question_text: A strip is divided into 6 equal parts. You shade 5 of them. What fraction represents the shaded portion?
questions.verified_explanation: 5 parts are shaded (numerator) out of 6 total equal parts (denominator), representing 5/6.
With equal numerators (3), dividing the whole into fewer pieces (5 parts) creates larger unit pieces than dividing into 7 parts. Thus, 3/5 > 3/7.

questions.question_text: What number must replace the question mark to make the fractions equivalent: 3/4 = ? / 12?
questions.verified_explanation: The denominator was multiplied by 3 (4 * 3 = 12). To remain equivalent, the numerator must also be multiplied by 3 (3 * 3 = 9). So 3/4 = 9/12.
questions.learning_objective: Generate equivalent fractions by multiplying by a common factor.

options: D) Neither, fractions cannot be compared when both numerator and denominator differ
questions.verified_explanation: To compare 3/7 and 4/9, find a common denominator (63): 3/7 = 27/63, and 4/9 = 28/63. Since 28/63 > 27/63, 4/9 is larger. Alternatively, cross-multiplication: 3 * 9 = 27 vs 4 * 7 = 28.
questions.learning_objective: Transfer fraction comparison to cases where both numerators and denominators differ.
